newsitem.title: USA: Pathologist releasing TWA victim autopsies.
newsitem.headline: Pathologist releasing TWA victim autopsies.

text.p: Autopsy reports on some victims of the TWA Flight 800 crash will be given to their relatives in the coming week, the chief medical examiner in the case said on Friday.
He said "about a third" of the autopsies on the bodies and remains of the 215 victims recovered from the Atlantic Ocean were being released at the request of the families and their attorneys.
The Boeing 747 exploded in mid-air off New York's Long Island without warning last July 17 just minutes after taking off for Paris, killing all 230 passengers and crew.

"The families have been asking for the autopsy reports for a variety of reasons, but we needed everyone's concurrence before we could release them," Dr. Charles Wetli, chief medical examiner of Suffolk County on Long Island, said.

Wetli said attorneys representing victim's relatives had requested the autopsy reports. Some relatives are preparing to sue TWA and the Boeing Co for the disaster, the cause of which has not yet been determined.
The National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Bureau of Investigation have said the tragedy could have been caused by a bomb, a missile or mechanical failure.

In November, top investigators said that with only five percent of the plane's wreckage yet to be recovered, there was less likelihood they will find that sabotage brought down the jetliner. Investigators know the plane's center fuel tank exploded but have not yet understood why.
Wetli said on Friday that the autopsy reports that were being released contained no new information on how the victims died.

"As I said earlier on, the victims lost conciousness immediately in the event or died directly from the explosion and it is a reasonable medical probability that virtually all died that way," Wetli said.

Wetli told a public hearing a month after the disaster that medical examiners found that most of the victims were killed quickly in mid-air by "phenomenal whiplash" that was "going to sever all function of the brain stem."
